question.problem:
Using the definition of the hyperbolic sine, calculate ${f}^{-1}(x)$ given that $f(x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\sqrt{x})$ for $x\ge 0.$

${f}^{-1}(x)=($
{{field-1}}$)^{2}$
question.worked_solution:
Let $y=\operatorname{sinh}⁡\sqrt{x}.$ Note that $f(x)$ is a one-to-one function on its entire domain. We have $y\in [0,\infty )$ for $x\in [0,\infty ).$

To find the inverse function we swap $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
x=\operatorname{sinh}⁡\sqrt{y},
$$

where $x\in [0,\infty )$ and $y\in [0,\infty ).$

Next, we apply the definition of $\operatorname{sinh}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{\sqrt{y}}-{e}^{-\sqrt{y}}) \\ 2x & ={e}^{\sqrt{y}}-{e}^{-\sqrt{y}} \\ 2x{e}^{\sqrt{y}} & ={e}^{2\sqrt{y}}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Bringing everything to the right-hand side, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2\sqrt{y}}-2x{e}^{\sqrt{y}}-1 & =0 \\ {({e}^{\sqrt{y}})}^{2}-2x({e}^{\sqrt{y}})-1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $Y={e}^{\sqrt{y}}.$ We can form a quadratic equation in $Y$ and solve it by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Y}^{2}-2xY-1 & =0 \\ (Y-x)^{2}-{x}^{2}-1 & =0 \\ (Y-x)^{2} & ={x}^{2}+1 \\ Y-x & =\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}+1} \\ Y & =x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}+1} \\ {e}^{\sqrt{y}} & =x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}+1} \\ \sqrt{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}) \\ y & ={ln}^{2}⁡(x\pm \sqrt{{x}^{2}+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we require real $y$ and $x<\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}$ for all $x,$ we select the positive solution. Therefore,

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)={(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}))}^{2}.
$$
